{{Short description|Jewish-German mathematician}}
'''Hermann Kober''' (born 1 February 1888 in [[Beuthen]],  Germany (now Bytom, Poland), died 4 October 1973 in Birmingham, England) was a [[Jewish-German]] mathematician who introduced [[Erdélyi–Kober operator]]s.
He taught (mathematics and science), up to the early 1960s, at some of the [[Foundation of the Schools of King Edward VI|King Edward VI Foundation]] schools in Birmingham.<ref>{{MacTutor|id=Kober|title=Hermann Kober}}</ref>
